summary: Today’s pulse tracks Politico reportedly barred from traveling with Trump amid administration’s crackdown on White House coverage – live, London to Chicago BA flight declares emergency after dropping 28,000 feet, and Obama to appear at Abdul El-Sayed rally in critical Michigan Senate race. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are first, progressive, and round. In the background, Trump says 'threat' led US to pull bombers from RAF Fairford and Flávio Bolsonaro poised to win Brazilian presidency after shock first-round victory keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Politico reportedly barred from traveling with Trump amid administration’s crackdown on White House coverage – live
headlines.description: White House did not let Politico on Air Force One, CNN reports; a federal judge had put a temporary block on Trump’s overall ban on Politico, CNN and MS Now But if the fossil fuel industry convinces the justices, the decision could apply not only to the Boulder case, but also to the many other climate cases brought by state and local governments around the US that we mentioned earlier.

headlines.title: London to Chicago BA flight declares emergency after dropping 28,000 feet
headlines.description: British Airways Boeing abruptly lost altitude over Ireland due to ‘technical issue’ and returned to Heathrow A flight from London to Chicago declared an emergency after a sudden and steep descent of 28,000 feet over Ireland and was forced to turn back to Britain. British Airways flight BA295 was bound for Chicago’s O’Hare airport but after a “technical issue” during which oxygen masks were deployed from the ceiling, the plane landed safely back at London Heathrow.

headlines.title: Obama to appear at Abdul El-Sayed rally in critical Michigan Senate race
headlines.description: Former president to visit 10 days before election day as victory for progressive challenger could tip Senate balance Barack Obama will head to Detroit this month to rally with Abdul El-Sayed, a show of establishment support for a progressive insurgent in Michigan, one of the most consequential Senate races in the country. The former president will appear with El-Sayed and the gubernatorial nominee, Jocelyn Benson, on 24 October, the state’s Democratic party announced on Monday. The rally falls on the first day of the state’s in-person early voting period and 10 days before election day.

headlines.title: Trump says 'threat' led US to pull bombers from RAF Fairford
headlines.description: The Pentagon confirmed on Sunday it had removed the B1 bombers from the base in England back to their home stations in America.

headlines.title: Flávio Bolsonaro poised to win Brazilian presidency after shock first-round victory
headlines.description: Progressive voters and supporters of incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva left reeling after far-right surge Flávio Bolsonaro is in pole position to win Brazil’s presidential election, after a far-right tsunami propelled him to a shock first-round victory over the incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, leaving progressive voters reeling. The 45-year-old rightwing candidate received 56.1m votes to Lula’s 53.8m – 47.03% to 45.16% – meaning the 80-year-old leftwinger has a mountain to climb if he is to bounce back in the second round on 25 October. Never, since the return of democracy to Brazil in 1985, has the first-round runner-up managed to turn the game around and win the second ballot.

headlines.title: Max Chandler-Mather pitches Mamdani-style $25bn plan to nationalise 200 Coles and Woolworths supermarkets
headlines.description: Former MP and Greens Institute head says proposal for publicly owned supermarket chain will ease grocery prices Channelling New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s plan for publicly owned grocery stores, Chandler-Mather, the head of the party’s thinktank, the Green Institute, wants to use new forced divestiture laws to take over major supermarket sites and three distribution centres. headlinePool.title: US 'watching closely' after plague researcher dies in Russia, Rubio says
headlinePool.description: The US says it is monitoring the case of a lab technician who died at a plague research centre in Siberia.

headlinePool.title: Students vandalize Cornell building over handling of gang-rape allegations
headlinePool.description: Student activists defend their actions as nonviolent, saying ‘property damage is not violent, condoning rape is’ Cornell University to take ‘serious look’ at fraternities after rape allegations Student activists vandalized a Cornell University administration building overnight in response to the university’s handling of gang-rape allegations in a high-profile case that has dominated national news. Students smashed a glass door at the entrance of Day Hall and painted messages on the walls at approximately 3am on Monday, the Cornell Daily Sun reported .

headlinePool.title: Saudi-backed forces recapture key areas around strait from Houthis in Yemen
headlinePool.description: Government offensive launched under air cover by Saudi military coalition aims to retake all Houthi-held territory Forces of the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen have recaptured several key areas around Bab al-Mandab strait from Iran-backed Houthi rebels, Yemeni officials said on Monday. The officials said forces allied with the internationally recognized government have retaken the crucial town of Dhubab just north of the strait. They also captured the towns of Bab and Hadeid, said the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to reporters. Witnesses said they saw government tanks and forces entering the towns.

headlinePool.title: Spain PM pins hopes on housing crisis to help win snap election
headlinePool.description: Calling of a snap election was not a knee-jerk reaction from Pedro Sánchez but a carefully thought-out manoeuvre, Guy Hedgecoe reports from Madrid.

headlinePool.title: Republicans criticize Steve Hilton for ‘creepy’ innuendo-filled campaign ad
headlinePool.description: Hilton faces heavy backlash from within his own party for ‘Just Try It’ ad amid his longshot bid for California governor Steve Hilton , the Republican candidate for California governor, is receiving heavy criticism from members of his own party over a controversial, sexual innuendo-filled campaign ad that has been described as “creepy”. The video entitled “Just Try It, California” was released last week and depicts two young women with brightly colored hair, sitting on a bed in front of a pride flag in low lighting. One nervously says “I can’t believe I’m doing this”, while another strokes her hair and coaxes “don’t be nervous, it’s not that bad” before guiding her to fill out a ballot for Hilton and aggressively commanding “lick it”.

headlinePool.title: Command-line tool quickly removes Apple Intelligence from macOS 27
headlinePool.description: The tool can free up over 12GB of storage.

headlinePool.title: Green party of England and Wales facing international ostracism over ‘Zionism is racism’ vote
headlinePool.description: European Green party says motion goes against its policy, with German Green co-leader calling it ‘intolerable and unacceptable’ Zack Polanski may rue lack of leadership when Greens needed him to act The English and Welsh Greens are facing international ostracism after adopting a policy declaring Zionism as a form of racism, which has drawn dismay from the group representing European Greens. The co-leader of the German Greens separately said the policy was “intolerable and unacceptable”, running contrary to its belief in the right of Israel to exist.

headlinePool.title: Tories are united behind Badenoch, but MPs want focus on economy over culture wars to win back voters
headlinePool.description: Party has common enemy in defectors, while Nigel Farage’s woes have given some insiders reason to hope During a quick-fire Q&A at the Conservative party conference this weekend, Kemi Badenoch was asked who she would pick between Robert Jenrick or Suella Braverman. “Why do you keep offering me these? It’s like asking if I’d rather be shot or drowned,” the Tory leader responded with her trademark directness.

headlinePool.title: Far right on the march and Lula’s failures: key drivers of Flávio Bolsonaro’s Brazil surge
headlinePool.description: Experts say strength of evangelical church and stubbornness of Lula, 80, also helped propel Jair Bolsonaro’s son to first-round election win On Sunday night, as the scale of the far-right triumph in Brazil sank in, an adapted football chant rang out in one of Rio’s most leftwing areas. “Let’s turn this around, Lu-laaaaa! Let’s turn this around, Lu-laaaaa! Let’s turn this around, Lu-laaaaa!” crestfallen progressives bellowed while drowning their sorrows after witnessing an excruciating election setback for their leader, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
